messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency breach detected for websocket cluster us-west-2-stream-01 — 2399s ongoing. Paging on-call.
maria: @here I'm oncall for infra. seeing p99 jump from 200ms -> 3s, p95 ~450ms. tons of stuck connections showing no progress on chunked frames.
tyler: adding logs — early signals look like a lot of connections in CLOSE_WAIT on the proxy level, and backend still returning data. suspect proxy stall/slow-flush.
sre-lead: if proxy is holding socket write due to client not reading (backpressure) we should see build-up in send buffers. can someone grab netstat/ss on host prox-03?
infra-bot: ran basic probe: prox-03: writes_pending=213, tx_queue_bytes=~18MB, keepalive-rtt ok. CPU and mem normal.
maria: grabbing ss now, output:
```
ESTAB 0 0 10.1.4.12:443 10.2.8.50:56744 timer:(keepalive,5min,0)
ESTAB 0 4096 10.1.4.12:443 10.3.7.99:53010 timer:(on,0,0)
```
shows a lot of tx_queue on some sockets.
lisa: customer-ops: getting a wave of support messages — several live-sessions report stalled assistant responses keeping them on loading state for >10s. no data loss, just long tail.
tyler: repro steps locally: open websocket, send prompt, server streams chunks but proxy buffers full and only flushes when client reads. some clients (mobile in particular) stop reading due to internal backpressure heuristics.
sre-lead: ok that means the root cause is slow clients + proxy write buffering + proxy keepalive/timeout interactions causing head-of-line stalls for other users. mitigation path: 1) reduce per-connection send buffer / enable chunk flush policy 2) fallback to short-polling for problematic clients 3) drain/bounce problematic proxy worker.
maria: I'm going to enable aggressive chunk flush on prox-03 via nginx config for streaming locations (proxy_send_timeout/proxy_buffering off, tcp_nodelay on). Pushing now.
```
# tentative config snippet
location /stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection '';
  proxy_send_timeout 30s;
}
```
infra-bot: config push queued to prox-03 canary slot.
tyler: adding temporary mitigation: patch server to set smaller SO_SNDBUF on new connections to limit memory amplification and force earlier backpressure signals to clients.
sre-lead: maria, once canary is up, can you route 10% of traffic to prox-03-canary and monitor p95/p99 for 15m? if stable, roll to 100%.
maria: canary live at 2399991145. routing rule: set header X-Canary: prox-03. Monitoring dashboards updated.
customer-ops: confirmed some affected sessions started to recover after canary — several users reported responses returning within 800-1200ms instead of >5s.
infra-bot: metrics: p99 for websocket_streaming across cluster dropped from 3.1s -> 1.1s on canary path; overall cluster p99 is 2.6s currently.
tyler: note — this is still a partial mitigation. we should also consider server-side consumer pacing: set chunk-size throttle and send keepalive comments to coax slow clients to read.
sre-lead: agreed. immediate next steps: 1) roll canary to 100% if no regressions (maria) 2) schedule a short restart of prox-03 workers to clear tx queues (maria) 3) create an alert filter to surface sockets with tx_queue > 1MB for >60s (tyler) 4) SRE follow-up postmortem to propose long-term fixes (connection-level backpressure metrics, per-client pacing, protocol-level acks).
maria: rolling canary to 100% now at 2399991168.
infra-bot: prox-03 workers drained and restarted at 2399991175; tx_queue cleared.
customer-ops: customers: two enterprise tenants reported improved latency; one mobile app still showing intermittent stalls, support already escalated with device logs.
lisa: filed customer incident update, tagging affected tenants and mitigation steps; suggested client update to read streaming chunks more aggressively as a short-term workaround.
tyler: I'll put a small hotfix for the server that adds periodic flush comments (\n:keepalive) every 500ms for slow streams — this should unblock proxy flush heuristics.
sre-lead: good. action items assigned. i'll take the postmortem and timeline. maria, monitor for 30m then start the impact assessment: count number of distinct affected users and estimate SLA exposure.
maria: will do. current cluster p95=420ms, p99=980ms. keeping channel updated.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: latency improved after proxy canary and worker restart. on-call handoff to next shift in 2h. Please document follow-ups and customer comms.
maria: handing off to tyler for overnight watch at 2399991188 — tyler, you have the pager.
tyler: taking the pager. will monitor the new tx_queue alert and follow up with client SDK team re: mobile read behaviour. :thumbsup:
